passages.provision_quote: the quantities shall reflect reasonable progress in each of the intervening years sufficient to ensure that the procurement of electricity products from eligible renewable energy resources achieves 25 percent of retail sales by December 31, 2016, 33 percent by December 31, 2020, 44 percent by December 31, 2024, 52 percent by December 31, 2027, and 60 percent by December 31, 2030
passages.note: Chaptered bill text: the operative section is a renewable-procurement mandate on retail sellers with dated targets, enforced by penalties.

rows.reasoning: Stern voted Aye on final concurrence in SB 100 (2017-2018), a single-subject clean-electricity bill whose operative section requires retail sellers to procure "electricity products from eligible renewable energy resources" reaching "44 percent by December 31, 2024, 52 percent by December 31, 2027, and 60 percent by December 31, 2030". That is a mandate on a named clean-energy source with firm deadlines, matching "Require a shift to clean energy through mandates and firm deadlines" and excluding the subsidy, permitting-and-grid, neutral and repeal rungs. The 25-13 tally is well short of near-unanimous.
